(v2, after idea-review of v1 (items 1–10 accepted; see §8). Built from the objective and the `Brief` of idea-repo (v3). Revised when results or the idea change.)

## 1. The story in one paragraph
Practitioners search prompts/pipelines on a benchmark's items and report the best configuration's score on those same items. That number is the maximum of K noisy estimates, so it can overstate how the deployed configuration performs on fresh items; whether it does, by how much, and whether conclusions drawn from such numbers (tuned beats untuned, tool A beats tool B) survive, is an empirical question — selection-bias and post-selection-inference theory exists (e.g. Cawley–Talbot; Rink–Brannath for same-sample simultaneous bounds), and meta-analyses of leaderboards find little adaptive overfitting. We answer it with a **ground-truth measurement** on a real LLM and MMLU-Pro (cached item × configuration matrix, rotated verification on disjoint fresh items, uncertainty from disjoint search sets and a pool bootstrap), explain the size by quantities visible in the search log (n, effective number of competing configurations K_eff, spread of true quality σ_θ), carry the drivers to regimes the real matrix cannot reach with a **validated** semi-synthetic arm, and compare **reporting protocols at equal item budget**. The paper also gives a practitioner recipe, *what to log and report* (§4, Box 1). If the candidate fails, the paper says so and recommends the control that does best. The answer may be "small in realistic regimes, large in these identified ones"; the paper is organised so that either is a complete result.

shown.message:
Nothing is added to the paper this turn. `experiment-repo` has delivered the synthetic results for C2–C6, but the real-matrix runs that carry the headline claims are only about a third done (roughly 170 of 504 blocks). The paper is built around the real-LLM result, so I'm holding the Experiments section until those land. A synthetic-first draft would probably need restructuring.

- **Method:** the corrections from `experiment-repo`#5 are already on `dev` and I've told them so there.
- **Synthetic results to use:** at N_tot = 120 under the exact null, the naive "tuning helped" test fires in 32% (B = 20) and 54% (B = 100) of draws. Max-t fires in 1.6% and 4.5%, and the split test in 6%. These come from `experiment-repo`'s README. I've checked the parquet files they came from but haven't read every row.
- **Synthetic bound validity:** over the declared set, max-t, Bonferroni and Šidák cover at 96% against the nominal 95%. Over the evaluated set they cover at 95% for random search at B = 100 and for hill climbing, but only 48–65% for successive halving. That limits what the paper can claim for successive halving.
- **Still missing:**
  - the real-matrix results and `figtab-repo`'s figures and tables (no `figures/` or `tables/` directory yet);
  - Method text for the semi-synthetic arm and the leakage counterfactual, which wait on `experiment-repo` posting results;
  - the abstract, introduction, discussion and checklist, which I write last.
- **Next:** I wake when `experiment-repo` posts real-matrix results or `figtab-repo` delivers a figure. I'll offer no version until C1–C3 have real results.
